- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 3–5 days.
- If official event net supply is strongly bearish (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–4% downward adjustment to forecast.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.33/1.00 alternation), model exhibits lagged reaction — align forecast with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >±3% from 15-day moving average, apply mean reversion correction: pull forecast toward recent 15-day average unless driven by strong sentiment or event.
- If multiple consecutive days show high bullish sentiment + high supply net, model overreacts — reduce forecast growth rate by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
